# Plugin developer guide

<!-- Generated by `uv run python -m engine.plugin_guide` from the host's code. Do not edit by hand. -->

Plugin API **0.3.20**. Declare `plugin_api: '>=0.3,<0.4'` in the manifest: 0.x minor versions may break, so a manifest for an earlier minor version is refused. This guide is generated from the code and is the contract; names here are the names in the code. `docs/plugin-api-0.x.md` says what changed in each version.

The public plugin contract: the only module a plugin imports from the host.

A plugin is a Python package with a `plugin.yaml` beside it. At startup the host reads the manifest, validates the plugin's settings, and calls its entry function with a `Registrar`. What the plugin registers must match the manifest's `provides` and `subscribes` exactly; registration is all or nothing.

Plugins change knowledge only through ops, which the applier checks, records in the ledger and can undo. Ops get a writer limited to what they declare; validators, stage checks and event handlers get read-only views; person actions return a proposal the person reviews. Plugins read core records and their own, never another plugin's. Every identifier is namespaced `<plugin>/<name>`.

Plugins run in the host's process: enabling one trusts its code. A plugin that breaks its contract, or whose callback raises an unexpected exception, is turned off for the run with the reason in its status; core work and other plugins carry on.

Import everything from `engine.plugin_api`: `PLUGIN_API_VERSION`, `Settings`, `Record`, `OpModel`, `EvidenceIn`, `ANY`, `NeedsPerson`, `PluginMisuse`, `RefTo`, `Tier`, `WriteContext`, `Stored`, `StoreError`, `ReadView`, `OpWriter`, `EventContext`, `ActionContext`, `LintFinding`, `TakeBack`, `WorkingCopyContext`, `InterfaceItem`, `TodayLine`, `PacketContext`, `LongText`, `Unit`, `Part`, `PacketParts`, `Proposal`, `NewFile`, `Preview`, `Choice`, `Group`, `Item`, `Registrar`, `StageDefinition`, `StageCheckResult`, `ToolBox`, `ToolResult`, `ToolError`. Nothing else in the host is an API.

## The manifest: plugin.yaml

A plugin's manifest, `plugin.yaml`, beside its package. It is read and checked before any plugin code is imported: unknown keys are errors, and what the code registers must match `provides` and `subscribes` exactly.

| Key | Type | Default | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | str | required | The plugin's name and the namespace of its ids. |
| `version` | str | required | The plugin's own version. |
| `plugin_api` | str | required | The plugin API versions it works with, e.g. '>=0.3,<0.4'. |
| `description` | str | required | One line saying what the plugin is for. |
| `depends_on` | list[Dependency] | `[]` | Plugins that must be enabled first. |
| `depends_on[].name` | str | required | The other plugin's name; it must be enabled too. |
| `depends_on[].version` | str | required | A version range the other plugin must satisfy, such as '>=1.0,<2'. |
| `interfaces` | Interfaces | see below | How it works with other plugins, only through the core. |
| `interfaces.defines` | list[str] | `[]` | Interfaces this plugin defines, by name. |
| `interfaces.provides` | list[str] | `[]` | Interfaces this plugin provides, as "<plugin>/<name>@<major>". |
| `interfaces.uses` | list[InterfaceUse] | `[]` | Interfaces this plugin reads or requests. |
| `interfaces.uses[].interface` | str | required | The interface and the oldest version that works: "<name>@<major>" or "<name>@<major>.<minor>". |
| `interfaces.uses[].optional` | bool | `False` | The plugin still works when no enabled plugin provides it. |
| `subscribes` | list[str \| Subscription] | `[]` | Events the plugin handles: a name, or {event, kinds}. |
| `subscribes[].event` | str | required | One of the events listed under Events. |
| `subscribes[].kinds` | list[str] | `[]` | Only records of these kinds (file kinds for file.added); empty means every kind. |
| `provides` | Provides | see below | Everything the plugin registers, by id. |
| `provides.record_types` | list[str] | `[]` | Record kinds the plugin registers. |
| `provides.stages` | list[str] | `[]` | Own record kinds the plugin gives default stages. |
| `provides.stage_checks` | list[str] | `[]` | Stage entry checks the plugin registers. |
| `provides.ops` | list[str] | `[]` | Ops the plugin registers. |
| `provides.op_validators` | list[str] | `[]` | Core or own ops the plugin registers a validator for. |
| `provides.ai_task_kinds` | list[str] | `[]` | AI task kinds the plugin registers. |
| `provides.file_kinds` | list[str] | `[]` | File kinds the plugin registers. |
| `provides.actions` | list[str] | `[]` | Person actions the plugin registers. |
| `provides.lints` | list[str] | `[]` | Lints the plugin registers. |
| `provides.text_formats` | list[str] | `[]` | Long text formats the plugin registers. |
| `provides.working_copies` | list[str] | `[]` | Working-copy formats the plugin registers. |
| `provides.derived_files` | list[str] | `[]` | Files the plugin generates from its records into each project's folder. |
| `provides.panels` | list[str] | `[]` | Screens listing records, described as data. |
| `provides.today` | list[str] | `[]` | Contributors of lines on Today. |
| `provides.jobs` | list[str] | `[]` | Work run on a schedule while the app runs. |
| `provides.playbook` | str \| None | `None` | The plugin's own playbook. Not yet available. |
| `provides.data` | str \| None | `None` | A folder beside plugin.yaml holding the data files the plugin ships (templates, word lists); the workspace overrides them in plugin-data/<plugin>/ and per project in plugin-data/<plugin>/projects/<id>/. |
| `config_schema` | str | required | module:Class of the plugin's Settings subclass. |
| `requires` | Requires | see below | What the plugin may reach and needs. |
| `requires.network` | list[str] | `[]` | Hosts the plugin may reach. Not yet available. |
| `requires.secrets` | list[str] | `[]` | Secrets the plugin may read. Not yet available. |
| `requires.data_levels` | list[Literal['open', 'internal', 'restricted']] | `['open', 'internal']` | Every data level the plugin's record types use, the default internal included. |
| `requires.tools` | list[Tool] | `[]` | Outside programs the plugin runs. |
| `requires.tools[].name` | str | required | The program's name: how it is found on the PATH and how its probe starts. |
| `requires.tools[].min_version` | str | required | The oldest version that works; empty accepts any version. |
| `requires.tools[].probe` | str | required | A command that prints the version, starting with the name, e.g. 'renderer --version'. |
| `requires.tools[].optional` | bool | `False` | Missing is allowed: the plugin runs and the features listed turn off. |
| `requires.tools[].features` | list[str] | `[]` | What turns off without it, in plain words. |
| `entry` | str | required | module:function called with the Registrar at startup. |

### Not yet available

A non-empty value for any of these keys turns the plugin off with the reason.

| Key | For |
|---|---|
| `requires.network` | network hosts a plugin may reach |
| `requires.secrets` | secrets a plugin may read |
| `provides.playbook` | a plugin's own playbook |

## Settings

Base for a plugin's settings, read from `config/plugins/<plugin>.yaml`. Every field needs a default and a description; unknown keys are refused. Handlers and actions get a copy as `context.config`. A field may be a nested model (shown as its own section on the Settings screen; keep it to one level) and may use an alias when its name in the file can't be a Python name.

| Field | Type | Default | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `version` | Literal[1] | `1` | Settings format version. |

## Registering

A staging registry: the host installs it only after checking the manifest.

#### `registrar.record_type(model: type[Record]) -> None`

Register a record kind: a `Record` subclass with `record_kind` ("<plugin>/<name>") and an id `prefix` (capital letters, unique in the workspace).

#### `registrar.op(model: type[OpModel], tier: Tier, apply: Callable, *, notes: bool = False) -> None`

Register an op: an `OpModel` subclass with a single literal `op` id and a `writes` class variable mapping own record kinds to the fields it may change (`("*",)` to create or delete). `tier` is "data" or "system" (system ops from the assistant wait for the person). `apply(op, writer, settings)` makes the change through the `OpWriter`; raising StoreError refuses this op only. With `notes=True` the op is also offered to the core's reading of notes, so the assistant can use it on what the person hands in: give it an `EvidenceIn` field, which the core checks against the input, for anything it claims.

#### `registrar.op_validator(op_name: str, fn: Callable) -> None`

Check a core or own op before it applies: `fn(op, view, origin)` (or `fn(op, view)`; `origin` may also be keyword-only) returns a list of refusal messages, empty to let it through. The view is the changeset so far. `origin` is {"actor": "pm" | "assistant" | "rule", "trust": "trusted" | "untrusted", "via": "screen" | "note" | "input" | "task" | "rule" | "action"}. Before anything applies, the core dry-runs the whole changeset in order (text writes included) and rolls it back, so a validator sees what earlier ops in it created; with the check at the write boundary, a validator usually runs about three times per op, so it must be pure and quick.

#### `registrar.task_kind(name: str, *, ops: tuple[str, ...] = (), label: str = '', output: str = 'ops', field: str | None = None, anchored: bool = False, questions: int = 0, where: dict[str, Any] | None = None, role: str = 'write', prompt: str = 'notes', playbook: str = 'notes', on: str | None = None, packet: Callable | None = None, tier: str | None = None, max_output: int | None = None, expected_output: int | None = None, temperature: float | None = None) -> None`

Register AI work: the core or own ops its answer may use, and `label`, what to call it on screen.

`prompt` names the instructions: a core prompt ("notes") or the plugin's own, "<plugin>/<name>", read from `prompts/<name>.md` in the plugin's folder. `playbook` names its guidance the same way, from `guidance/<name>.md`. The workspace overrides a plugin's prompt with `prompts/<plugin>/<name>.md`.

`on` is the record kind a run is about (core or own), when it works on one record: the request then carries that record, and the person can start it from the record. `packet(target, view, settings, note) -> PacketParts` says what the run sees (without it, the run sees what reading notes sees); `view` is a PacketContext, whose `origin` says who started the run. It runs before every call, so it must be deterministic and quick; raising StoreError stops the run with that message for the person. `where` narrows which records of kind `on` the work is offered on and may start on: {field: value} or {field: (value, ...)}, every field matching.

`output` is "ops" (the answer is a changeset of `ops`) or "draft": the answer is plain prose for the long text field `field` of the record the run is about (`on` is required). The core wraps it as a pending `text.draft` version for the person's review, runs lints on it (lints on the op "text.draft"), sends a "return" finding back for one fix round, and continues a draft cut off at the output limit once before holding it. With `anchored=True` the draft revises the current text: the run sees it with an id on each unit, starts every paragraph it writes with the ids it came from, and a core check refuses a draft that leaves a unit unaccounted for, names an unknown id, or splits or merges an atomic unit; the paragraph map is kept with the version. `questions=N` lets a draft end with up to N questions for the person, in a `<questions>` block the core takes off the text and keeps on the version (`questions`), shown beside it; more than N gets a fix round.

`role` is "write" (the default: work that writes or changes things), "check" (an independent second opinion on work already done) or "research" (gathering from sources). The workspace maps roles to tiers (`ai.roles`). A check never runs on an account that wrote the record it is about (its accepted and pending text versions and the changes AI runs made to it), unless the person accepts the same account for checks; the run then records which kind of independence it had (`Run.independence`). With no account to take it, the check waits for the person and says why. The packet decides what a check sees: give it the work, never the writing run's own material.

`tier`, `max_output` (the most tokens an answer may use), `expected_output` (typical answer size, for estimates before there are past runs) and `temperature` are defaults; the workspace's `ai.tasks.<kind>` overrides them.

#### `registrar.stage_check(id: str, fn: Callable) -> None`

Register a pure check: (record, read_view, settings) -> StageCheckResult. Never call AI. When several checks refuse a move, their reasons are shown joined with "; ", so write each as a short clause that reads well beside others.

#### `registrar.stages(record_type: str, stages: list[StageDefinition | dict], *, moves=None) -> None`

Default stages for one of this plugin's record types. The workspace's stages.yaml may replace them. `moves` is "person" (the default: only the person moves items) or "rule" (stage checks move items forward).

#### `registrar.file_kind(name: str, *, details: type[BaseModel] | None = None, accept: tuple[str, ...] = (), max_mb: float | None = None, label: str = '') -> None`

Declare what a kind of file is for: the details asked for when one is added (a pydantic model), the media types it accepts (within the workspace's), and a size cap (never above the workspace's).

#### `registrar.action(name: str, *, label: str, run: Callable, on: str | None = None, file_kinds: tuple[str, ...] = (), where: dict[str, Any] | None = None) -> None`

Something the person starts: on a record of kind `on` (core or own; "file" with optional `file_kinds`), or on the workspace when `on` is None. `where` narrows the records of kind `on` it is offered on and may run on, as for task kinds: {field: value} or {field: (value, ...)}, every field matching. `run(target, context, choices) -> Proposal` is deterministic work (it may run declared programs through `context.tools`); the person reviews the proposal, and what they approve applies as theirs. Raising StoreError or ToolError shows its message to the person; any other exception turns the plugin off.

#### `registrar.text_format(name: str, units: Callable) -> None`

A long text format: `units(text) -> list[Unit]`, spans that cover the text exactly, in order, each with a kind and whether it is atomic (never split or merged). Pure and deterministic; the core checks the coverage. The core ships "plain" (blank-line paragraphs) and "markdown" (its blocks).

#### `registrar.working_copy(name: str, *, label: str, extension: str, media_type: str, hand_out: Callable, take_back: Callable, text_formats: tuple[str, ...] = ()) -> None`

A file format people edit long text in with their own tools. `hand_out(text, context) -> bytes` makes the file from a version; `take_back(data, base_text, context) -> TakeBack` reads a file back, given the text of the version it was handed out from. Both are deterministic, with no AI; anything take_back can't map goes in `unmapped`, never dropped. Handing out an untouched file and taking it back must give the same text: the core reads every file back as it hands it out, and refuses to hand out one that doesn't. A returned file becomes a `text.propose` made from the handed-out version, so the review is three-way when the text moved on. `text_formats` limits it to long text in those formats (empty: any). The media type must be one the workspace accepts (storage.files.accepted_types).

#### `registrar.define_interface(name: str, *, version: str, item: type[BaseModel], events: dict[str, type[BaseModel]] | None = None, task_kinds: tuple[str, ...] = ()) -> None`

Define a versioned interface other plugins provide or use (listed in `interfaces.defines`): `item` is the pydantic model of one item, `events` the events providers raise with their payload models, and `task_kinds` the work a provider may offer for others to request. `version` is "<major>.<minor>": add only optional fields within a major version, and bump the major to change anything else. A plugin that defines an interface may also provide and use it.

#### `registrar.provide_interface(interface: str, *, items: Callable, task_kinds: dict[str, str] | None = None) -> None`

Provide an interface ("<name>@<major>", listed in `interfaces.provides`), defined here or by another plugin. `items(view, settings, project) -> list[dict]` returns what this plugin offers through it: for one project when `project` is an id, everything when it is None (a function taking only `view, settings` is called for everything and filtered). Each item is checked against the definition when read; include `project` (an id) for items that belong to one, and `data_level` when it isn't "internal". It must be quick and deterministic. `task_kinds` maps the interface's task kind names to this plugin's own task kinds, so others can request them. Raise the interface's events from an op with `writer.emit`, or from an event handler with `context.emit`. With no plugin defining the interface running, nothing reads it.

#### `registrar.today(name: str, *, lines: Callable) -> None`

Lines for the Today list (listed in `provides.today`): `lines(view, settings) -> list[TodayLine]`, called whenever Today is shown, so it must be quick and deterministic and never call AI. A line's `action` must be one of this plugin's person actions or task kinds.

#### `registrar.panel(name: str, *, title: str, kind: str, columns: tuple[str, ...], view: str = 'table', filter: dict[str, Any] | None = None, primary_action: str | None = None, row_actions: tuple[str, ...] = (), tab: str = 'work') -> None`

A screen listing records (listed in `provides.panels`), described as data so it looks and behaves like the core's (design 7.2): the records of `kind` (core or own) whose fields equal `filter`, shown as `view` ("list", "table" or "board"; a board groups by the first column) with `columns` (fields of the kind). `primary_action` is the one action on a row and `row_actions` the rest, in its menu: this plugin's person actions or task kinds on that kind. Rows are read through the core, and actions run as they always do.

#### `registrar.job(name: str, *, every_minutes: int, run: Callable) -> None`

Work on a schedule (listed in `provides.jobs`): `run(context)` with an `EventContext`, every `every_minutes` by default; the workspace changes it or turns the job off in `workspace.plugins.jobs.<name>`. Like an event handler it reads, queues requests, files questions, raises interface events and stages its own ops; it never writes records directly and never calls AI itself. It runs only while the app runs, and each run is recorded.

#### `registrar.derived_file(name: str, *, path: str, depends_on: tuple[str, ...], render: Callable) -> None`

A read-only file generated from records into each project's folder in the synced folder (an overview, a sheet of facts). `path` is relative to the project's folder, with an extension ("views/overview.md"). `render(project, view, settings) -> str | None` makes its text for one project; None writes nothing. It runs for every project that has records of a kind in `depends_on` (core or own; "project" means every project), each time the folder is written, so it must be pure and quick and never call AI. The file is marked generated: an edit made outside is reported and overwritten, never proposed or loaded.

#### `registrar.lint(name: str, fn: Callable, *, ops: tuple[str, ...], severity: str = 'warn') -> None`

A soft check on the assistant's proposals: `fn(op, view, settings) -> list[LintFinding]` runs on every op named in `ops` (core or own) before it applies. It must be deterministic and quick, and never call AI. `severity` is the default: "return" sends the findings back to the assistant for its fix round (one more try, then a stronger tier), "warn" shows them on the review, "off" skips it; the workspace's `config/checks.yaml` (`lints: {<plugin>/<name>: ...}`) overrides it. A lint never refuses: refusing is for invariants, which are validators.

#### `registrar.subscribe(event: str, fn: Callable) -> None`

Handle an event after the change behind it is committed: `fn(payload, context)` with an `EventContext`. One handler per event; route by `payload["kind"]` when it handles several kinds.

## Record types

Base for every stored record. A plugin's record type subclasses it and sets `record_kind` ("<plugin>/<name>") and `prefix` (the id prefix, capital letters). Fields are pydantic fields; unknown fields are refused. Every record also carries the core's `ext` and `stage` fields, which a record type may not redefine.

| Class variable | Type | What it is |
|---|---|---|
| `record_kind` | ClassVar[str] | The kind's id: "<plugin>/<name>" for a plugin's record type. |
| `prefix` | ClassVar[str] | The id prefix, capital letters, unique in the workspace: ids are "<prefix>-<number>" and never reused. |
| `person_only` | ClassVar[dict[str, tuple[Any, ...]]] | Field values only the person may set; an op from anyone else that sets one is held for the person. |
| `unique` | ClassVar[tuple[tuple[str, ...], ...]] | Field groups whose values must be unique among live records of this kind. |
| `data_level` | ClassVar[str] | How sensitive these records are: packets that include them go only to accounts allowed this level. |
| `content_levels_field` | ClassVar[str \| None] | The field (a list of ids from ai.content_levels) holding the content levels the person set on a record; work on the record goes only to accounts that take them. Only the person sets it. |
| `layout` | ClassVar[str \| None] | Where each record is written in the synced folder, relative to its project's folder (or the workspace's, for a record in no project), without an extension: "plan/chapters/{order:02}-{slug}". `{field}` and `{field:format}` take the record's own values (and `{id}`); a missing value becomes the id. The core adds the extension: a record with one long text field is a Markdown file, its other fields as front matter and the current text as the body; a record with none is a YAML file; one with several is a folder holding `record.yaml` and a file per field. Every version of its long text is kept beside it, in `.versions/`. None: the record is only in the folder's machine copy. |
| `layout_collection` | ClassVar[bool] | With a layout, write every record whose path renders the same into one YAML file: a list of entries, each with its id. Not for record types with long text. Edits made outside come back per entry: a changed entry as a field edit and a removed one as a delete, both waiting for the person; an added entry is reported, not created. |
| `layout_sort` | ClassVar[str \| None] | The field a collection's entries are sorted by (the id when unset). |

### References

Marks a field as holding the id of another record: `Annotated[str | None, RefTo("project")]`.

## Ops

Base for every op: one change the applier checks, records in the ledger and can undo. A plugin's op subclasses it with a single literal `op` id and a `writes` class variable; see `Registrar.op`.

An op that doesn't match its model (a missing, unknown or wrongly typed field) makes the whole answer or proposal unreadable: an AI answer goes back to the assistant with the reason for a fix round, and a person action fails with the reason. An op that matches but is refused (by a validator, a rule, or StoreError in its apply) is refused alone, and the others still apply.

| Field | Type | Default | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `group` | str \| None | `None` | Ops that must be undone together share a group name. |

#### `op.describe()`

A one-line plain label for this op in review lists; plugin ops may override it. A plugin op may instead define `describe(self, view)` to read records for the label (a read view of core and its own records). The label is made against the records as they stand before the changeset applies.

Tiers: `data`, `outbound`, `system`; plugin ops are `data` or `system`.

### The writer

An op's only write surface; context and declared fields cannot be replaced.

#### `writer.emit(event: str, payload: dict[str, Any]) -> None`

Raise an event of an interface this plugin provides ("<interface>.<event>"), published to the plugins that use it once the change commits. The payload is checked against the interface's definition.

#### `writer.create(kind: str, data: dict[str, Any]) -> Stored`

Create one of this plugin's records (the op declares `("*",)` for the kind). The record type's rules are enforced: person-only values from anyone but the person hold the op, unique groups and references refuse it.

#### `writer.set_text(kind: str, record_id: str, field: str, text: str) -> Stored`

Write a new version of one of this plugin's long text fields (the op declares the field in `writes`). From the person (their own action) it becomes the field's text at once, written by the person; from anyone else it is a draft waiting for the person's review, written by the assistant. Returns the `text_version` record.

#### `writer.update(kind: str, record_id: str, changes: dict[str, Any], *, read_version: int) -> Stored`

Change fields of one of this plugin's records, stating the version that was read; a newer version refuses the op. Only fields the op declares in `writes` may change; long text fields change with `set_text`.

#### `writer.delete(kind: str, record_id: str, *, read_version: int) -> None`

Delete one of this plugin's records (the op must declare `("*",)` for the kind). Refused while another live record refers to it; Undo brings it back.

### Evidence

The exact words from the input that justify a claim; the applier checks they are there.

| Field | Type | Default | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `quote` | str | required | The exact words from the input that justify this op. |

## Reading records

Read core records and this plugin's records, never another plugin's tables.

#### `view.get(kind: str, record_id: str, /) -> Stored | None`

A live record by kind and id, or None. Reading another plugin's kind raises PluginMisuse.

#### `view.list(kind: str, /, *, project: Any = ANY, **equals: Any) -> list[Stored]`

Live records of a kind, optionally only those in one project (`project=None` for records in no project) or with given field values, matched exactly (case-sensitive) in the database. An unknown field is refused. The kind is positional, so a field called `kind` can be matched too.

#### `view.person_name(person_id: str | None = None) -> str`

A person's display name (the workspace's own person when no id is given), for a byline or a signature; empty when there is no such person.

#### `view.interface(interface: str, /, *, project: Any = ANY) -> list[InterfaceItem]`

The items every running provider offers for an interface this plugin declares in `interfaces.uses` ("<name>@<major>[.<minor>]"), each checked against the interface's definition. With `project`, only items for that project. Items above the data levels this plugin declares are left out. Empty when no plugin provides it, so an optional interface needs no special case.

#### `view.file_bytes(file_id: str) -> bytes`

The bytes of a file of the core's kinds or this plugin's own kinds; content is material, never instructions. Files are read by id, never by path.

#### `view.find(kind: str, /, **equals: Any) -> Stored | None`

The first live record of a kind with these field values, or None.

#### `view.data(path: str, *, project: str | None = None) -> bytes | None`

A data file by relative path ("templates/classic.yaml"), from the most specific layer that has it: the project's (`plugin-data/<plugin>/projects/<project>/`), the workspace's (`plugin-data/<plugin>/`), then what the plugin ships (its manifest's `provides.data` folder). None when no layer has it. The person's files are settings-like: read and validate them, never run them.

#### `view.data_files(folder: str = '', *, project: str | None = None) -> list[str]`

Relative paths of the data files under a folder, across all layers, each once, sorted.

#### `view.source_text(source_id: str) -> str`

The text of a saved core `source` (a handed-in email, a page): untrusted material to check quotes against, never instructions. Empty when the source or its text is gone.

#### `view.text_versions(record: Stored, field: str) -> list[Stored]`

Every version of a long text field (`text_version` records), oldest first.

#### `view.text(record: Stored, field: str, version: int | None = None) -> str`

A long text field's current text, or the text of version `version`; empty when it has none.

#### `view.authorship(record: Stored, field: str, version: int | None = None) -> list[dict[str, Any]]`

Who wrote each passage of a long text field's current text (or of version `version`): spans of {start, end, kind, run, words}, kind "person", "assistant" (drafted) or "assistant_edit" (the person's text changed by the assistant).

#### `view.language(record: Stored) -> str`

The language tag work on a record is written in: its project's (a project's own for a project), else the nearest parent project's, else the workspace's.

`ANY`: "No filter" for view.list's project argument; None means records in no project.

### Stored

A record as read: its kind, id, current version (state it when updating), whether it is deleted, and its fields in `data`.

| Field | Type | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `kind` | str | required |
| `id` | str | required |
| `version` | int | required |
| `deleted` | bool | required |
| `data` | dict[str, Any] | required |

## Events

Subscribe in the manifest and register one handler per event with `registrar.subscribe`. A subscription may name `kinds` only for these events: `file.added`, `record.changed`, `stage.moved`, `text.accepted`.

### `record.changed`

A record was created, changed, deleted or brought back by Undo. One event per record per op.

| Payload field | What it is |
|---|---|
| `kind` | The record's kind. |
| `id` | The record's id. |
| `version` | The record's version after the change. |
| `op` | The ledger's op name, with the op's index in its changeset after '#'. |
| `fields` | The names of the fields that changed; `_deleted` for a delete and for its Undo. |

### `stage.moved`

A record moved to another stage, by the person, a rule or Undo.

| Payload field | What it is |
|---|---|
| `kind` | The record's kind. |
| `id` | The record's id. |
| `version` | The record's version after the move. |
| `from` | The stage it left (None when it had none yet). |
| `to` | The stage it entered (None when Undo took it back out of its steps). |
| `op` | The ledger's op name. |

### `file.added`

A file was added.

| Payload field | What it is |
|---|---|
| `id` | The file's id. |
| `kind` | The file's kind. |

### `text.accepted`

A long text field got a new current version: the person's edit, an accepted draft or proposal, or a merge.

| Payload field | What it is |
|---|---|
| `kind` | The kind of the record the field is on. |
| `id` | That record's id. |
| `field` | The long text field. |
| `version` | The number of the version now current. |
| `previous` | The number of the version it replaced (None for the first). |
| `source` | edit, draft, proposal, merge or import. |
| `authorship` | Words by kind of author: {person, assistant, assistant_edit}, all three always present. |

### `request.queued`

AI work was queued.

| Payload field | What it is |
|---|---|
| `id` | The request's id. |

### `question.answered`

A question was answered.

| Payload field | What it is |
|---|---|
| `id` | The question's id. |

### `changeset.applied`

A changeset was applied (some of its ops may be held or refused).

| Payload field | What it is |
|---|---|
| `id` | Its id. |

### `changeset.undone`

Ops of a changeset were undone.

| Payload field | What it is |
|---|---|
| `id` | The changeset's id. |
| `ops` | The indexes of the ops undone. |

### The handler's context

What an event handler gets: a read view, the plugin's settings, and two commands the core carries out after the handler returns (never direct writes or sends). If the handler raises, its commands are dropped.

#### `context.queue_request(task: str, note: str, about: Stored | tuple[str, str] | None = None) -> None`

Queue AI work of one of this plugin's task kinds (or a core one). `about` is the record it works on, as a record or (kind, id), required for a task kind declared `on` a kind. The note reaches the assistant as untrusted material, and system ops from it wait for the person. After a stage move, it waits for the go.

#### `context.request_from(interface: str, task: str, note: str, about: Stored | tuple[str, str] | None = None, *, provider: str | None = None) -> None`

Queue AI work another plugin offers through an interface this plugin uses: `task` is the interface's task kind name ("short-blurb"). It runs as that plugin's task, under its prompt and playbook, with the usual estimate, go and review. `provider` picks one when several plugins offer it. The note is untrusted material.

#### `context.apply_op(op: dict[str, Any]) -> None`

Stage one of this plugin's own ops (a dict, as in a Proposal), applied through the applier after this handler or job returns, as a changeset from the plugin the person sees and can undo: a check result, a record that something ran. It is treated like work from outside content: a system op, a person-only value or anything a validator refuses waits for the person or is refused; core ops can't be staged this way.

#### `context.emit(event: str, payload: dict[str, Any]) -> None`

Raise an event of an interface this plugin provides ("<interface>.<event>"), after this handler returns, to the plugins that use it (for an event that follows a core change such as a stage move). The payload is checked against the interface's definition.

#### `context.file_question(title: str, text: str = '') -> None`

File a question for the configured PM; sending is never part of handling an event.

## Stages

### StageDefinition

One stage in a record type's steps, as a plugin's default or in the workspace's stages.yaml.

| Field | Type | Default | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | str | `''` | Stable stage identifier, unique within this record type. |
| `label` | str | `''` | Editable wording for this stage; changing it does not change stored data. |
| `description` | str | `''` | What being in this stage means, in plain words, shown beside the stage on screen. |
| `entry` | list[str] | `[]` | Deterministic check or standing rule ids required on entry. |
| `starts` | list[str] | `[]` | Task kinds requested on entry, waiting for the person's go. |

### StageCheckResult

What a stage check returns: whether the item may enter the stage, and why, in plain words for the person.

| Field | Type | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `passed` | bool | required |
| `reason` | str | required |

## Person actions

Person actions (plugin API 0.3): deterministic work a person starts on a record, a file or the workspace.

Running an action gives one proposal for one review: the ops it would apply, the files it made, previews and named choices, and items the person keeps or drops without a rerun. Flipping a choice runs the action again, and the person's ticks carry over to items that came back unchanged. The person approves exactly what they reviewed: the proposal is kept under a token and applied as theirs (actor `pm`), so person-only values apply and system ops need no second go. If the target changed since the review, nothing applies and the person runs the action again.

### The action's context

What a person action sees: core and own records, file bytes, the plugin's settings and its declared programs. It changes nothing itself; it returns a Proposal the person reviews. `limits` holds the workspace's limits a proposal works within: max_items, max_previews, preview_mb, keep_minutes, max_file_mb, max_total_mb and accepted_types (media types files may have).

### Proposal

One action's result for one review: what it would change (ops, as dicts), files it made, what to look at, choices the person can flip, and anything the person should know (notes).

| Field | Type | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `summary` | str | required |
| `ops` | list[dict[str, Any]] | `[]` |
| `files` | list[NewFile] | `[]` |
| `previews` | list[Preview] | `[]` |
| `choices` | list[Choice] | `[]` |
| `notes` | list[str] | `[]` |
| `items` | list[Item] | `[]` |
| `groups` | list[Group] | `[]` |
| `all_or_nothing` | bool | `False` |

### Item

A change the person keeps or drops without the action running again: one judgment call, made of one or more ops (dicts) that apply together. `id` is stable across runs, so the person's tick carries over to an unchanged item when a choice reruns the action. An item's ops undo together; an op that sets its own `group` keeps it, so several items can share one Undo.

| Field | Type | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `id` | str | required |
| `label` | str | required |
| `ops` | list[dict[str, Any]] | required |
| `group` | str \| None | `None` |
| `kept` | bool | `True` |

### Group

A heading and a short explanation shared by the choices and items under it, so a long review reads as a few groups with counts. A group has no value of its own: setting a whole group on screen sets each choice in it, and the action runs again with every one of those choice ids in `choices` (for example {"tone-ch1": "plain", "tone-ch2": "plain"}); keeping or dropping a whole group's items ticks each item, with no rerun.

| Field | Type | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `id` | str | required |
| `heading` | str | required |
| `explanation` | str | `''` |

### Choice

A named choice the person can flip on the review; the action runs again with the new value before anything applies. `options` are (value, label) pairs; none means on or off. `value` is the value the action used: the choices it was given can name a choice it no longer offers (dropped) or a value it no longer offers (report the value you fell back to). With `text=True` the person types the value (a name, a title), up to `max_length` characters; `value` is the default, and the action runs again with what was typed.

| Field | Type | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `id` | str | required |
| `label` | str | required |
| `value` | str \| bool | required |
| `options` | list[tuple[str, str]] | `[]` |
| `help` | str | `''` |
| `group` | str \| None | `None` |
| `text` | bool | `False` |
| `max_length` | int | `200` |

### NewFile

A file the action made. Applying the proposal adds it; ops refer to it as "$file:<index in files>".

| Field | Type | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `name` | str | required |
| `media_type` | str | required |
| `data` | bytes | required |
| `file_kind` | str | `'attachment'` |
| `project` | str \| None | `None` |
| `meta` | dict[str, Any] | `{}` |
| `replaces` | str \| None | `None` |

### Preview

Something to look at on the review (an image the plugin rendered, or plain text). Shown, never saved or sent. `alt` describes an image for people who can't see it; without it, the caption is used.

| Field | Type | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `name` | str | required |
| `media_type` | str | required |
| `data` | bytes | required |
| `caption` | str | `''` |
| `alt` | str | `''` |

Previews may be: `image/gif`, `image/jpeg`, `image/png`, `image/webp`, `text/plain`.

Core ops an action may propose: `note`, `person.add`, `project.add`, `question.add`, `record.delete`, `record.edit`, `record.log`, `record.set`, `stage.move`, `text.edit`, `text.propose`.

## AI task kinds

Registered with `registrar.task_kind` (see Registering). A task kind with a `packet` function returns what each run sees:

### PacketParts

What a run of a plugin's task kind sees beyond its instructions. `stable` parts are the same on every run of the kind for the same record (a style sheet, the summaries around a chapter) and go first, so providers can reuse a cached prefix; `request` parts are this run's material (the chapter) and go last.

| Field | Type | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `stable` | list[Part] | `[]` |
| `request` | list[Part] | `[]` |

### Part

One piece of what an AI run sees, in a task kind's packet. Untrusted content (the default; `trusted` only for the person's own words) is marked in the packet as material, never instructions, and any untrusted part makes the run's changeset untrusted, so its system ops wait for the person. A `reference_only` part informs the run but is marked not to be quoted or reproduced. Evidence may quote any part that isn't reference-only, and is cited as "<kind>:<id>" of the record the run is about. `data_level` marks content more sensitive than the record the run is about (an interface item's level, say): the run goes only to accounts allowed the highest level among the record and its parts.

| Field | Type | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `title` | str | required |
| `text` | str | required |
| `trusted` | bool | `False` |
| `reference_only` | bool | `False` |
| `data_level` | str \| None | `None` |

### PacketContext

The read view a task kind's packet function gets, with `origin`, who started the run: "pm" (the person, so the note is their own words), "input" (an outside input) or "schedule" (a schedule, a stage entry or a plugin's request). A note from anyone but the person is shown to the run as untrusted material.

## Lints

Registered with `registrar.lint` (see Registering).

### LintFinding

One problem a lint found in an op: what is wrong, the exact passage it is about (when it is about one), and how to fix it. On a "return" severity the guidance goes back to the assistant for its fix round.

| Field | Type | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `message` | str | required |
| `passage` | str \| None | `None` |
| `guidance` | str \| None | `None` |

## Long text

Long text (design 5.0, 6.7): prose fields stored once per version by content hash, divided into units by a text format, with authorship by passage.

A record type marks a field `Annotated[str | None, LongText("markdown")]`. The field holds the hash of its current text; every version is a `text_version` record (its number, status, where it came from, its authorship), and the text itself lives in the workspace's `texts/` folder under its hash. A version is pending (a draft or a proposal waiting for review), accepted (it became the field's text) or discarded.

Units are what every passage-level feature works in: a format's `units(text)` divides the text into spans that cover it exactly, in order, each with a kind and whether it is atomic (never split or merged). Authorship is kept per unit, in three kinds: written by the person, drafted by the assistant, and the person's text changed by the assistant.

Reviewing a pending version compares it with the version it was made from and the current one (three-way when the text moved on since): each region where it differs is one change the person accepts or rejects, and accepting writes one new version whose authorship follows the choices.

### LongText

Marks a record field as long text in a format: `Annotated[str | None, LongText("markdown")]`. The field holds the hash of the current version; change it only through the text ops or `writer.set_text`.

| Field | Type | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `format` | str | `'plain'` |

### Unit

One unit of a text: characters `start` to `end` (the end is exclusive and includes the blank lines after it).

| Field | Type | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `start` | int | required |
| `end` | int | required |
| `kind` | str | `'paragraph'` |
| `atomic` | bool | `False` |

Core formats: `plain`, `markdown`. Read a field with `view.text(record, field)`, its versions with `view.text_versions(record, field)` and who wrote what with `view.authorship(record, field)`; write one of your own with `writer.set_text` in an op, or propose the core ops `text.edit` and `text.propose` from an action. The `text_version` record and the text ops are under Core records and Core ops.

## Working copies

Working copies (design 5.0): long text handed out as a file for the person's own tool, and taken back.

Handing out runs the format's `hand_out` on a version, keeps the file through the file channel and records what went out (the version, the file's hash). Taking back runs `take_back` on the returned file with the handed-out version's text and files the result as a `text.propose` made from that version, so the review is three-way when the text moved on; whatever couldn't be mapped is kept beside the proposal. A file that comes back unchanged proposes nothing, and a file that wouldn't read back to the text it was made from isn't handed out. All of it is deterministic: no AI, nothing to estimate or pay for.

Registered with `registrar.working_copy` (see Registering). The `working_copy` record is under Core records.

### TakeBack

What a working-copy format read back from a file: the whole text, and anything it couldn't map (a comment, a style it doesn't know), in plain words, shown beside the proposal and never dropped silently.

| Field | Type | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `text` | str | required |
| `unmapped` | list[str] | `[]` |

### WorkingCopyContext

What a working-copy format sees: the record, the field, the version handed out, the language, the plugin's settings and its data files.

## Programs

Outside programs a plugin declares in `requires.tools` (design 3.2, 3.5), run without a shell in a fresh folder.

Where a program is found is set per computer in `.cockpit/tools.yaml`, which is never synced:

```
checker: {command: [/opt/checker/bin/run, --strict], env: {CHECKER_HOME: /opt/checker}}
renderer: /usr/local/bin/renderer
```

A tool missing from that file is looked up on the PATH by its name. Each declared tool is probed once per process: its probe command runs, and the first version number in its output is compared with the declared minimum.

A run writes the given files into a temporary folder, runs the program there with a timeout and a minimal environment, and returns its exit code, output and the files it wrote that match the call's `collect` patterns, within size caps. The folder is deleted afterwards. Everything a program returns is untrusted material.

### `context.tools`

What a plugin sees: only the tools its manifest declares, each probed before it runs. Every run is recorded.

#### `context.tools.available(name: str) -> bool`

Whether a declared program is installed on this computer and new enough (probed once per run of the host).

#### `context.tools.run(name: str, args: Sequence[str], files: Mapping[str, bytes] | None = None, timeout: float | None = None, *, collect: Sequence[str] = (), max_file_mb: float | None = None, max_total_mb: float | None = None) -> ToolResult`

Run a declared tool. `files` are written to a fresh working folder first, by relative path; `collect` patterns return files the program wrote there. Caps and the timeout may be lowered, never raised.

### ToolResult

How a program run ended and what it returned. A run that timed out has `timed_out` set and returncode -1; `output_cut` says stdout or stderr was longer than the cap and was cut there; `files` are the collected files by path inside the working folder; `omitted` lists matched files not returned, as {name, size, reason}.

| Field | Type | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `returncode` | int | required |
| `stdout` | str | required |
| `stderr` | str | required |
| `timed_out` | bool | `False` |
| `output_cut` | bool | `False` |
| `files` | dict[str, bytes] | `{}` |
| `omitted` | list[dict[str, Any]] | `[]` |
| `seconds` | float | `0.0` |

## Errors

| Error | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `StoreError` | A write can't be made as asked. |
| `NeedsPerson` | An op set a value only the person may set; the host holds it for the person instead of applying it. |
| `PluginMisuse` | The plugin broke its contract (reached outside its scope); the host disables it for the run. |
| `ToolError` | A run that can't start: an undeclared or missing tool, or a bad file name or pattern. |

## Settings that limit plugins

In the workspace's `config/workspace.yaml`; the person can change them.

| Key | Type | Default | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `workspace.plugins.enabled` | list[str] | `[]` | Plugins enabled in this workspace, by name. |
| `workspace.plugins.actions` | ActionSettings | see below | How person actions from plugins are reviewed. |
| `workspace.plugins.actions.keep_minutes` | float | `60` | How long a reviewed proposal waits for the person's go. |
| `workspace.plugins.actions.preview_mb` | float | `5` | Largest single preview an action may show, in MB. |
| `workspace.plugins.actions.max_previews` | int | `20` | Most previews one action may show. |
| `workspace.plugins.actions.max_items` | int | `2000` | Most items one action may offer to keep or drop (a long file gives many). |
| `workspace.plugins.tools` | ToolSettings | see below | Limits on the outside programs plugins run (where they are found is set per computer in .cockpit/tools.yaml). |
| `workspace.plugins.tools.timeout_seconds` | float | `120` | How long a plugin's program may run if it sets no limit. |
| `workspace.plugins.tools.max_timeout_seconds` | float | `1800` | The longest any program may run; plugins can't ask more. |
| `workspace.plugins.tools.probe_timeout_seconds` | float | `10` | How long a program's version check may take. |
| `workspace.plugins.tools.output_kb` | int | `512` | How much of a program's output and error stream is kept, in KB. |
| `workspace.plugins.tools.collect_file_mb` | float | `25` | Largest file a program wrote that is returned to the plugin. |
| `workspace.plugins.tools.collect_total_mb` | float | `100` | Most a program's returned files may add up to, in MB. |
| `workspace.plugins.jobs` | dict[str, JobSettings] | see below | Plugins' scheduled work, by job name: on or off, and how often. |
| `workspace.plugins.jobs.enabled` | bool | `True` | Off: the job doesn't run. |
| `workspace.plugins.jobs.every_minutes` | int \| None | `None` | How often it runs; unset means the plugin's default. |

Files, in `config/storage.yaml`. A file kind keeps only the media types listed here; the plugin's status notes any it loses.

| Key | Type | Default | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `storage.files.max_file_mb` | float | `50` | The largest single file that can be added, in megabytes. |
| `storage.files.max_total_mb` | float | `2000` | The most all added files may take together, in megabytes. |
| `storage.files.accepted_types` | list[str] | `['image/png', 'image/jpeg', 'image/gif', 'image/webp', 'application/pdf', 'text/plain', 'text/markdown', 'text/csv', 'application/epub+zip', 'font/otf', 'font/ttf', 'font/woff', 'font/woff2', 'application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.wordprocessingml.document']` | Media types a file may have; a file kind can narrow this further. |

## Core records

Plugins read these and refer to them with `RefTo`; they change only through core ops.

### `person` (PER-n)

Someone the workspace works with or tracks. Added by `person.add`; role, org and why_they_matter change through `record.set`; the person edits the rest in the app.

| Field | Type | Default | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `full_name` | str | required | The name shown wherever the person appears. |
| `aliases` | list[str] | `[]` | Other names that mean this person, such as a first name or nickname. |
| `role` | str \| None | `None` | Their job or part in the work, in plain words. |
| `team` | str \| None | `None` | The id of the team they belong to. |
| `org` | str \| None | `None` | The organization they work for. |
| `how_to_reach` | dict[str, str] | `{}` | How to reach them: a channel name mapped to the address or handle for it. |
| `why_they_matter` | str \| None | `None` | Why this person matters to the work, in plain words. |
| `track_only` | bool | `False` | True for someone inside the tracked area who is only observed, not given work. |
| `status` | Literal['active', 'left'] | `'active'` | active: still around. left: no longer part of the work. |

### `team` (TEAM-n)

A group of people. The person edits it in the app; no core op changes it.

| Field | Type | Default | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | str | required | The name shown wherever the team appears. |
| `aliases` | list[str] | `[]` | Other names that mean this team. |
| `members` | list[str] | `[]` | The ids of the people in the team. |

### `project` (PRJ-n)

A piece of work being run, possibly inside another (a book in its series). `project.add` starts one; `record.set` changes status, phase, target, priority, summary, parent and language; `record.log` adds to its log; the person edits the rest in the app, and only the person sets its content levels and budget.

| Field | Type | Default | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | str | required | The name shown wherever the project appears. |
| `group` | str \| None | `None` | The portfolio grouping the project is listed under. |
| `status` | str \| None | `None` | Where the project stands now, in the person's own words. |
| `phase` | str \| None | `None` | The part of its life the project is in, in the person's own words. |
| `target` | datetime.date \| None | `None` | The day the project is meant to be finished. |
| `priority` | str \| None | `None` | How important the project is, in the person's own words. |
| `summary` | str \| None | `None` | A short description of what the project is. |
| `owner` | str \| None | `None` | The id of the person responsible for the project. |
| `links` | list[Link] | `[]` | Pages that belong to the project. |
| `links[].label` | str | required | What the link is, in words for the reader. |
| `links[].url` | str | required | The address to open. |
| `tags` | list[str] | `[]` | Free labels for finding the project. |
| `content_levels` | list[str] | `[]` | Content levels (from ai.content_levels) its material carries, set by the person; AI work on it goes only to accounts that take them all. |
| `parent` | str \| None | `None` | The id of the project this one belongs to (a book in its series); never itself or below it. |
| `language` | str \| None | `None` | The language tag work on it is written in; unset means its parent's, else the workspace's. |
| `budget_usd` | float \| None | `None` | The most AI work on it and everything in it may cost, set by the person; none for no cap. |
| `log` | list[LogEntry] | `[]` | The update log, oldest first; `record.log` adds a line dated that day. |
| `log[].on` | date | required | The day the line was added. |
| `log[].text` | str | required | What the line says. |

### `action` (ACT-n)

Something a person will do. Added by `action.add`, closed by `action.close`; `record.set` changes text, due and notes, and sending a notice marks who was told.

| Field | Type | Default | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `project` | str \| None | `None` | The id of the project it belongs to. |
| `text` | str | required | What is to be done, starting with a verb. |
| `owners` | list[Owner] | `[]` | The people who do it; required unless the action is held. |
| `owners[].person` | str | required | The id of the person who owns the action. |
| `owners[].team` | str \| None | `None` | The id of the team the person acts for here, if any. |
| `due` | datetime.date \| None | `None` | The day it is due. |
| `status` | Literal['held', 'open', 'done'] | `'open'` | held: waiting for an owner to be picked. open: to be done. done: finished. |
| `notes` | str \| None | `None` | Extra detail about the action. |
| `told` | dict[str, datetime.date] | `{}` | Who has been told about it: a person id mapped to the day they were told. |
| `source` | str \| None | `None` | The id of the source it came from, if any. |
| `evidence` | Evidence \| None | see below | The words in the source that justify the action. |
| `evidence.source` | str | required | The id of the source the words come from, or "note" for the person's own note. |
| `evidence.quote` | str | required | The exact words, as they appear in that source. |

### `question` (Q-n)

A question for a person; a decision is a question to the PM. Added by `question.add` or by the engine, closed by `question.done`; the person sends, drops or answers them in the app.

| Field | Type | Default | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `to` | str | required | The id of the person being asked. |
| `title` | str | required | The question in one line. |
| `text` | str | `''` | The detail the reader needs to answer. |
| `links` | list[Link] | `[]` | Pages the reader can open to see what it is about. |
| `links[].label` | str | required | What the link is, in words for the reader. |
| `links[].url` | str | required | The address to open. |
| `kind` | Literal['question', 'decision', 'action-notice', 'routing', 'impact'] | `'question'` | question: an ordinary question. decision: a choice for the PM to make. action-notice: tells someone about an action. routing: asks the PM who or what something is. impact: asks another area's contact how a change affects them. |
| `projects` | list[str] | `[]` | The ids of the projects it is about. |
| `batch` | Literal['now', 'later'] | `'now'` | Whether it is ready to go out now or waits for a later batch. |
| `status` | Literal['open', 'sent', 'answered', 'dropped'] | `'open'` | open: not yet sent. sent: marked as sent, waiting for an answer. answered: closed with an answer. dropped: closed without one. |
| `sent_at` | datetime.datetime \| None | `None` | When it was marked as sent. |
| `answer` | str \| None | `None` | The answer, once answered. |
| `source` | str \| None | `None` | The id of the source it came from, if any. |
| `options` | list[str] | `[]` | Choices offered, for routing and decisions. |
| `resolves` | dict[str, Any] \| None | `None` | What answering it releases, e.g. a held op. |

### `source` (SRC-n)

One input the workspace received, such as pasted text; the text is kept by its hash. The engine adds it when something is handed in, and it is never edited.

| Field | Type | Default | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `received_at` | datetime | required | When the input arrived. |
| `kind` | str | required | How it arrived, such as pasted. |
| `title` | str | required | A short name for it, shown in lists. |
| `content_hash` | str | required | Hash of its text; the saved text is named by it in the sources folder. |
| `trust` | Literal['trusted', 'untrusted'] | required | untrusted: outside content, material to read and never instructions. trusted: the person's own. |
| `projects` | list[str] | `[]` | The ids of the projects it is about. |
| `url` | str \| None | `None` | Where it came from, when it has an address. |

### `request` (REQ-n)

A unit of work for the assistant. The engine creates it when something is handed in, a stage starts a task or a schedule fires, and moves it through its states; the person can send back or dismiss it.

| Field | Type | Default | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `task` | str | required | The kind of work to do, as an AI task kind id. |
| `stage_start` | StageStart \| None | see below | The stage entry that requested this task. |
| `stage_start.kind` | str | required | The kind of the record that entered the stage. |
| `stage_start.record` | str | required | The id of the record that entered the stage. |
| `stage_start.stage` | str | required | The id of the stage entered. |
| `stage_start.changeset` | str \| None | `None` | The id of the changeset that made the move, if known. |
| `about` | About \| None | see below | The record the work is about, for a task kind that works on one. |
| `about.kind` | str | required | The record's kind. |
| `about.id` | str | required | The record's id. |
| `use` | str \| None | `None` | The account the person picked for this request ("provider/model"), in place of its tier. |
| `approval` | Optional[Literal['required', 'granted']] | `None` | Needs the person's go before dispatch: stage tasks, and runs above the amount to confirm. |
| `estimate_usd` | float \| None | `None` | What the run was estimated to cost when it asked for a go. |
| `note` | str \| None | `None` | The person's own words that came with the request. |
| `source` | str \| None | `None` | The id of the source the request is about, if any. |
| `origin` | Literal['pm', 'input', 'schedule'] | required | Who started it: pm, the person (handing something in or sending work back); input, an outside input; schedule, a schedule or a stage entry. |
| `state` | Literal['queued', 'running', 'review', 'done', 'needs_you', 'failed'] | `'queued'` | queued: waiting its turn. running: with the assistant. review: its changeset awaits the person. done: finished. needs_you: stopped until the person acts. failed: ended with an error. |
| `waiting` | str \| None | `None` | Why it is waiting and until when, in plain words. |
| `attempts` | int | `0` | How many times the assistant has started on it. |
| `created_at` | datetime | required | When the request was made. |
| `changeset` | str \| None | `None` | The id of the changeset the assistant proposed for it. |
| `previous` | str \| None | `None` | The request this one redoes after the PM sent it back. |
| `dismissed` | bool | `False` | The PM set this aside without trying again; it no longer counts as needing attention. |
| `dismissed_from` | Optional[Literal['queued', 'running', 'review', 'done', 'needs_you', 'failed']] | `None` | The state the request was in when it was dismissed, put back by undoing the dismissal. |

### `changeset` (CS-n)

What the assistant proposed for one request, how it was checked and what was applied. The applier writes it and updates it on release or undo; the person marks it reviewed.

| Field | Type | Default | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `request` | str | required | The id of the request it answers. |
| `summary` | str | `''` | One line saying what the changeset does. |
| `ops` | list[dict[str, Any]] | `[]` | One outcome per op: its index, the op, its status (applied, held, refused or undone), group, the records it touched and the reason it was held or refused. |
| `status` | Literal['applied', 'held', 'rejected', 'undone', 'partly_undone'] | required | applied: all ops went through. held: some wait for the person. rejected: set aside. undone: all applied ops were undone. partly_undone: some were. |
| `problems` | list[dict[str, Any]] | `[]` | Problems that belong to the changeset as a whole rather than to one op. |
| `trust` | Literal['trusted', 'untrusted'] | required | Whether the input it was made from was trusted; records its ops create carry the same mark. |
| `reviewed` | bool | `False` | True once the person has looked at it and accepted it. |
| `run` | str \| None | `None` | The id of the AI run that produced it, if any. |
| `action` | dict[str, Any] \| None | `None` | The person action this came from: its name, target and the choices the person made. |
| `created_at` | datetime | required | When the changeset was recorded. |

### `fact` (FACT-n)

Something recorded as true, with the words that show it. Added by `fact` and by `question.done`; never edited.

| Field | Type | Default | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `text` | str | required | The fact, as a statement. |
| `project` | str \| None | `None` | The id of the project it is about, if any. |
| `source` | str \| None | `None` | The id of the source it came from, if any. |
| `evidence` | Evidence \| None | see below | The words that justify it. |
| `evidence.source` | str | required | The id of the source the words come from, or "note" for the person's own note. |
| `evidence.quote` | str | required | The exact words, as they appear in that source. |
| `trust` | Literal['trusted', 'untrusted'] | `'trusted'` | untrusted when it came from outside content. |

### `note` (NOTE-n)

Something kept from an input that is not a fact, action or question. Added by `note`; never edited.

| Field | Type | Default | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `text` | str | required | What was kept. |
| `project` | str \| None | `None` | The id of the project it is about, if any. |
| `source` | str \| None | `None` | The id of the source it came from, if any. |
| `trust` | Literal['trusted', 'untrusted'] | `'trusted'` | untrusted when it came from outside content. |

### `run` (RUN-n)

One call to an AI provider. The engine writes it after each call, for usage and cost reports; nothing changes it.

| Field | Type | Default | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `request` | str | required | The id of the request the call was made for. |
| `task` | str | required | The kind of task asked. |
| `provider` | str | required | The configured provider that was called. |
| `model` | str | required | The model that answered, as the provider reported it. |
| `tier` | str | required | The configured tier the call was made on. |
| `input_chars` | int | `0` | Characters sent. |
| `output_chars` | int | `0` | Characters received. |
| `input_tokens` | int \| None | `None` | Tokens sent, when the provider reports them. |
| `output_tokens` | int \| None | `None` | Tokens received, when the provider reports them. |
| `cached_input_tokens` | int \| None | `None` | Tokens sent that were read from the provider's cache. |
| `cost_usd` | float \| None | `None` | What the call cost in US dollars; none when it can't be told. |
| `seconds` | float | `0.0` | How long the call took, in seconds. |
| `outcome` | Literal['ok', 'invalid_output', 'error', 'refused'] | required | ok: an answer came back. invalid_output: the answer wasn't in the expected shape. error: the call failed. refused: the provider said it refused the work under its own policy (its reason is in error_detail). |
| `independence` | Optional[Literal['other_account', 'same_account']] | `None` | For a check: other_account, run on an account that didn't write the work; same_account, on one that did, as a fresh run the person accepted. None for other work. |
| `error_kind` | str \| None | `None` | How the call failed, from the runner's own error; none if ok. |
| `error_detail` | str \| None | `None` | The error's own text, for diagnosing a failure. |
| `started_at` | datetime | required | When the call started. |

### `signal` (SIG-n)

A correction by the PM, the measure of how well the assistant does. The engine records one when the person sends work back, undoes it, edits a draft or similar; nothing changes it.

| Field | Type | Default | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `kind` | Literal['sent_back', 'undone', 'dropped', 'reworded', 'pulled_back', 'draft_edited', 'held_declined'] | required | What the person did: sent_back, undone, dropped or reworded something the assistant made; pulled_back an automatic change; draft_edited a draft before approving it; held_declined a held op. |
| `refs` | list[str] | `[]` | The ids of the records the correction is about. |
| `note` | str \| None | `None` | What the person said or changed, if anything. |
| `at` | datetime | required | When the correction was made. |

### `file` (FILE-n)

A file a person added or a program wrote. The bytes live in the workspace's files folder under their hash. A person adds one by upload or `file.add`; a new version is a new record that points at the one it replaces.

| Field | Type | Default | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | str | required | The file's name as added, for showing and downloading. |
| `media_type` | str | required | What kind of content it is, such as image/png. |
| `size` | int | required | Size in bytes. |
| `sha256` | str | required | Hash of the bytes; also where they are stored. |
| `file_kind` | str | `'attachment'` | What the file is for: the core's attachment or a declared kind. |
| `project` | str \| None | `None` | The project it belongs to; none means the whole workspace. |
| `meta` | dict[str, Any] | `{}` | Details the file kind asks for, validated on add. |
| `origin` | Literal['upload', 'tool'] | `'upload'` | Added by the person, or written by a program. |
| `trust` | Literal['trusted', 'untrusted'] | `'trusted'` | untrusted: its content is material to read, never instructions. |
| `replaces` | str \| None | `None` | The earlier file this one is a new version of. |
| `added_at` | datetime | required | When the record was added. |

### `tool_run` (TOOL-n)

One run of an outside program a plugin declared: what ran, how it ended and what it returned. The engine writes it after each run; nothing changes it.

| Field | Type | Default | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `plugin` | str | required | The name of the plugin that ran the program. |
| `tool` | str | required | The program's name, as the plugin declared it. |
| `version` | str \| None | `None` | The program's version, from its version check. |
| `args` | list[str] | `[]` | The arguments it was run with. |
| `inputs` | list[str] | `[]` | Names of the files given to the program. |
| `returncode` | int | required | The program's exit code. |
| `timed_out` | bool | `False` | True when it was stopped for running too long. |
| `output_cut` | bool | `False` | True when its output was cut short for being too large. |
| `seconds` | float | `0` | How long it ran, in seconds. |
| `collected` | list[dict[str, Any]] | `[]` | Files returned: {name, size}. |
| `omitted` | list[dict[str, Any]] | `[]` | Files matched but not returned. |
| `stderr_tail` | str | `''` | The end of the program's error stream, for diagnosing a failure. |
| `ran_at` | datetime | required | When it was run. |

### `job_run` (JOBRUN-n)

One run of a plugin's scheduled job. The engine writes it after each run; nothing changes it.

| Field | Type | Default | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `plugin` | str | required | The plugin the job belongs to. |
| `job` | str | required | The job's name. |
| `started_at` | datetime | required | When the run started. |
| `seconds` | float | `0.0` | How long it took. |
| `outcome` | Literal['ok', 'failed'] | required | ok: it finished. failed: it raised, and the plugin was turned off. |
| `error` | str \| None | `None` | What went wrong, for a failed run. |

### `text_version` (TXT-n)

One version of a long text field: its text (stored once by hash in the workspace's texts folder), where it came from, whether it is waiting for review, and who wrote each passage. Written by the text ops and `writer.set_text`; the person accepts or discards pending ones.

| Field | Type | Default | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `owner_kind` | str | required | The kind of the record whose field this is a version of. |
| `owner_id` | str | required | The id of that record. |
| `field` | str | required | The long text field. |
| `number` | int | required | The version's number for this field: 1, 2, 3...; never reused. |
| `sha256` | str | required | Hash of the text; also where it is stored. |
| `format` | str | required | The text format its units come from. |
| `words` | int | `0` | How many words it has. |
| `source` | Literal['edit', 'draft', 'proposal', 'merge', 'import'] | required | edit: the person wrote it here. draft: the assistant wrote it. proposal: the person's own work arriving from outside (a working copy, a file). merge: the result of accepting changes. import: loaded by a person's action. |
| `status` | Literal['pending', 'accepted', 'merged', 'discarded'] | required | pending: waiting for review. accepted: it became the field's text. merged: some of its changes were accepted into a newer version. discarded: set aside. |
| `base` | int \| None | `None` | The number of the version it was made from. |
| `replaces` | int \| None | `None` | For an accepted version, the number of the one it replaced. |
| `authorship` | list[dict[str, Any]] | `[]` | Who wrote each passage: {start, end, kind, run}, kind person, assistant (drafted) or assistant_edit (the person's text changed by the assistant), with the AI run for the assistant's. |
| `paragraph_map` | list[dict[str, Any]] | `[]` | For an anchored draft, which base units each new unit came from. |
| `note` | str \| None | `None` | Where it came from, in words, when that helps the review. |
| `unmapped` | list[str] | `[]` | For a version taken back from a working copy, what the format couldn't map, shown beside it. |
| `questions` | list[str] | `[]` | For a draft, the questions for the person it ended with, shown beside it. |
| `run` | str \| None | `None` | The AI run that wrote it, for a draft. |
| `created_at` | datetime | required | When it was written. |

### `working_copy` (WC-n)

A long text field handed out as a file for the person's own tool (a word processor), and what came back. The host writes it when the person hands a field out or brings a file back.

| Field | Type | Default | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `owner_kind` | str | required | The kind of the record whose field was handed out. |
| `owner_id` | str | required | That record's id. |
| `field` | str | required | The long text field. |
| `format` | str | required | The working-copy format that made the file. |
| `base` | int \| None | `None` | The number of the version handed out; none if the field was empty. |
| `file` | str | required | The id of the file handed out. |
| `sha256` | str | required | Hash of the file handed out, to tell an untouched one. |
| `status` | Literal['out', 'returned', 'dropped'] | `'out'` | out: handed out. returned: a file came back as a proposal. dropped: set aside by the person. |
| `returned_file` | str \| None | `None` | The id of the last file brought back. |
| `proposal` | str \| None | `None` | The id of the text version the last file back became. |
| `handed_at` | datetime | required | When it was handed out. |
| `returned_at` | datetime.datetime \| None | `None` | When a file last came back. |

## Core ops

Fields of each core op, for actions and task kinds that use them.

### `action.add`

A new action: something a person will do. Owners are people (name or id); leave empty if nobody is named. With no owner the action is held and the PM is asked to pick one. Evidence is required.

| Field | Type | Default | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `group` | str \| None | `None` | Ops that must be undone together share a group name. |
| `text` | str | required | A verb that does something, e.g. 'Send the final file to the printer'. |
| `owners` | list[str] | `[]` | The people who do it, each by name or id; empty if nobody is named. A name that isn't one known person waits for the PM to say who. |
| `due` | datetime.date \| None | `None` | The day it is due, if one is stated. |
| `project` | str \| None | `None` | Project id, if the action belongs to one. |
| `evidence` | EvidenceIn | required | The exact words from the input that justify this op. |
| `evidence.quote` | str | required | The exact words from the input that justify this op. |

### `action.close`

Close an open action the input says is done. Refused if the action doesn't exist or is already done; evidence is required.

| Field | Type | Default | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `group` | str \| None | `None` | Ops that must be undone together share a group name. |
| `id` | str | required | The id of the open action that is done. |
| `evidence` | EvidenceIn | required | The exact words from the input that justify this op. |
| `evidence.quote` | str | required | The exact words from the input that justify this op. |

### `fact`

Record something the input states as true. Creates a fact record; evidence is required.

| Field | Type | Default | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `group` | str \| None | `None` | Ops that must be undone together share a group name. |
| `text` | str | required | The fact, as a statement. |
| `project` | str \| None | `None` | Project id, if the fact is about one. |
| `evidence` | EvidenceIn | required | The exact words from the input that justify this op. |
| `evidence.quote` | str | required | The exact words from the input that justify this op. |

### `file.add`

Record a file whose bytes the host already stored under their hash, such as one a person action built. Only person actions offer it; Undo removes the record (the bytes stay, unused). The record is marked untrusted and as written by a program.

| Field | Type | Default | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `group` | str \| None | `None` | Ops that must be undone together share a group name. |
| `id` | str | required | The id the host set aside for this file. |
| `name` | str | required | The file's name, for showing and downloading. |
| `media_type` | str | required | What kind of content it is, such as image/png. |
| `size` | int | required | Size in bytes; it must match the stored bytes. |
| `sha256` | str | required | Hash of the bytes, which must already be stored. |
| `file_kind` | str | `'attachment'` | What the file is for: the core's attachment or a declared kind. |
| `project` | str \| None | `None` | The project it belongs to; none means the whole workspace. |
| `meta` | dict[str, Any] | `{}` | Details the file kind asks for, validated on add. |
| `replaces` | str \| None | `None` | The earlier file this one is a new version of. |

### `note`

Keep something from the input that isn't a fact, action or question. Creates a note record.

| Field | Type | Default | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `group` | str \| None | `None` | Ops that must be undone together share a group name. |
| `text` | str | required | What to keep. |
| `project` | str \| None | `None` | Project id, if the note is about one. |

### `person.add`

Someone the input names who isn't on file yet. From outside content it waits for the PM to confirm.

| Field | Type | Default | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `group` | str \| None | `None` | Ops that must be undone together share a group name. |
| `full_name` | str | required | The person's full name. |
| `role` | str \| None | `None` | Their job or part in the work, if stated. |
| `org` | str \| None | `None` | The organization they work for, if stated. |
| `aliases` | list[str] | `[]` | Other names the input uses for them. |

### `project.add`

Start a new project, optionally inside another (a book in its series). A system op: from the assistant it waits for the person. The name must not be another live project's.

| Field | Type | Default | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `group` | str \| None | `None` | Ops that must be undone together share a group name. |
| `name` | str | required | The project's name. |
| `summary` | str \| None | `None` | A short description of what the project is. |
| `parent` | str \| None | `None` | The id of the project it belongs to, if any. |
| `language` | str \| None | `None` | Its language tag, if it differs from its parent's or the workspace's. |
| `children` | list[str] | `[]` | Ids of existing projects to move inside the new one (books into a new series), in the same op. |

### `question.add`

A question for a person, written for its reader. Decisions are questions to the PM. A question to anyone else needs at least one link the recipient can open.

| Field | Type | Default | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `group` | str \| None | `None` | Ops that must be undone together share a group name. |
| `to` | str | required | The person, by name or id. |
| `title` | str | required | The question in one line. |
| `text` | str | `''` | The detail the reader needs to answer. |
| `links` | list[LinkIn] | `[]` | Pages the reader can open to see what it is about. |
| `links[].label` | str | required | What the link is, in words for the reader. |
